jobs.name: pelagic-coastal-district-v6
jobs.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: CORPORATE BRUTALIST science-fiction game art direction reference, screenshot paintover.
INPUT 1 is the actual existing game screenshot and EDIT TARGET. Preserve its camera, aspect ratio, horizon, landscape geometry, original vegetation, lighting and blue daytime sky. Remove the debug HUD. Build the new architecture into this existing terrain; do not stylize the natural world into low poly, upgrade its trees, replace the mountains, or change the weather.
The user specifically wants the DARK CORPORATE CONCRETE mood they associate with Anarchy Online. Earlier concepts were too cozy, friendly and frontier-rustic. This must be a major architectural change: severe, monolithic, impersonal corporate power, dense heavy concrete, institutional repetition, intimidating scale, vast blank walls, deep recesses, and visibly controlled movement. Its darkness must come from charcoal/basalt-colored concrete, dark green-gray materials and deep architectural shadow, NOT from turning the scene into nighttime or darkening the whole screenshot.
Design language: massive stepped and offset slab volumes, thick structural piers, blunt cantilevers, tall recessed vertical slots, narrow strip windows, heavy service doors, concrete retaining walls, enclosed bridges, brutalist modular facade bays. Smooth modest bevels and moderately detailed hard-surface game geometry, clean major forms that can be made from repeated Blender modules. Broad material stains, rain streaks, old patched seams, worn institutional markings. Avoid masses of tiny greebles or fine wire clutter. Technology is unmistakably futuristic through monumental proportions, sealed transit links, recessed industrial equipment and controlled access terminals.
Palette: dark charcoal and graphite concrete dominate, dark oxidized green or steel blue secondary, dirty pale concrete at some joints, sparse cold white or cyan task lights in deep shade, small restrained amber hazard markers. One stark off-white corporate marking, text exactly 'PELAGIC', in plain uppercase institutional typography. Buildings should look maintained but indifferent to individual comfort. Rust is localized rather than covering everything.
No cafes, cozy awnings, inviting porch lights, rooftop gardens, cheerful market stalls, village prefabs, decorative palms, rustic sheds, colorful patchwork facades or friendly cream/teal resort styling. No soldiers fighting, ruined apocalypse, gothic fantasy, faceted low-poly landscape, neon cyberpunk signs, captions, border or watermark. Ordinary employees and vehicles establish scale. Keep the surrounding natural environment under the original bright daylight.
SCENE: a dark corporate coastal district owned by Pelagic Works.
The source has open sea on the left and beach rising on the right. Occupy the RIGHT half of the composition with a visually dominant mass of corporate urban architecture, including near-to-camera right-edge structures as well as the skyline. Preserve the left-hand open water, its horizon, the source mountain silhouette wherever not occluded, and a strip of original beach in the near foreground.
A huge charcoal concrete headquarters slab rises over a terraced administration/housing complex. One broad asymmetric cantilever casts a deep shadow over a recessed transit entrance. Repeating tall narrow window recesses cut the headquarters facade; a few deep cyan-white interior strips reveal occupied floors. Company name 'PELAGIC' is monumental but austere on a blank vertical wall. Adjacent lower blocks are severe stepped corporate housing/office bars with no decorative balconies, raised on thick piers above a shadowed service concourse.
An enclosed elevated transit tube links the blocks. The coastal edge is a high stained retaining wall and restricted service quay with a utilitarian cargo lift, a squat dark company transport and an access gate. A checkpoint funnels small groups of workers through a narrow controlled entrance below overwhelmingly large walls. One or two angular light masts and camera/sensor boxes show surveillance without turning this into a military base.
Communicate hierarchy through vertical scale and the contrast between enormous blank concrete surfaces and tiny employees. The architecture should dominate the right skyline and feel heavy, cold and oppressive even on this sunny coast. Do not produce another pleasant Mediterranean waterfront with dark paint. Entire building proportions, access routes, structural mass and public-space treatment must carry the corporate mood.

SCENE: a company-controlled terraforming administration and processing compound on an open frontier plain.
Preserve the original open terrain, sparse trees and right-hand distant mountain ridge. A straight worn concrete access road runs from the lower center into a formidable checkpoint. The compound occupies the center-left middle distance, close and large enough that workers, gate mechanisms and structure are legible.
Main structure: a broad DARK CHARCOAL concrete administrative/processing slab lifted on enormous piers, with a heavy offset upper storey cantilevering over the gate forecourt. Narrow recessed window strips, a few giant dark louvered equipment bays, vertical structural fins and deep rectangular cutouts. A lower wing extends into identical plain employee housing blocks. On one side an exposed but orderly service area contains two massive dark tank volumes and thick utility trunks disappearing through the wall. A simple tall instrument mast, enclosed transit bridge and heavy freight door provide the futuristic identity.
At the entrance, two monumental concrete gate pylons and a low guard/control kiosk constrict movement. Concrete dividers separate pedestrian badge access from a lane for a blunt company freight vehicle. A small queue of ordinary workers, an employee standing at a terminal and a few stark cold-white fixtures inside the shaded gateway establish institutional routine. Company marking 'PELAGIC' sits high over the approach. Almost no personal decoration. Forecourt surfaces are patched and stained; the machinery is operational.
Architecture is massive, repetitive and economical to build from slabs, piers, recessed bays and repeated modules. This should feel like arriving at an employer that owns the roads, housing and essential infrastructure, not at an independent roadside settlement. Do not copy a prison, contemporary bunker or oil refinery; retain a distinctive futuristic corporate-brutalist silhouette and civilian industrial purpose. Keep open natural land visible around the oppressive man-made compound.
